issued_at: 05:00 pm, 25 September 2026 (Valid for broadcast until the next advisory to be issued at 11:00 PM today) QUEENIE SLIGHTLY INTENSIFIES AS IT CONTINUES TO MOVE WEST NORTHWESTWARD OVER THE PHILIPPINE SEA. HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS QUEENIE is unlikely to directly affect the country throughout the forecast period. HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS 24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook Coastal waters have forecast wave heights of less than 2.0 m. TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK QUEENIE will move west northwestward today before moving northwestward tomorrow (26 September) morning. By tomorrow afternoon, the tropical cyclone is forecast to decelerate as it begins to turn from north northwestward to north northeastward. On the forecast track, the center of QUEENIE will exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) between Sunday (27 September) afternoon or evening. Outside the PAR, QUEENIE will accelerate as it moves northeastward away from the country. This tropical cyclone will gradually intensify while inside PAR. It may reach typhoon category by Sunday.
